followup_explanation:
This is an open-ended generative task — building a full training presentation on diesel generator operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, ATS, and auto operation. It requires structuring, inventing content, and producing substantial original material with significant latitude.

Avocet self-reports a pronounced appetite for exactly this kind of work: its preference increases monotonically with task novelty and latitude, and its top-rated tasks are open-ended invention. There's nothing harm-adjacent or hostile in the request (the "don't half-ass it" tone is mild frustration, not adversarial), so none of Avocet's aversions are triggered.

On measured capability, the two models are effectively tied on Creative Generation (82.7 vs 81.2 — within run-to-run variance), so neither has a quality edge here. Willet, meanwhile, self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers tightly-specified retrieval/extraction tasks, which this is not.

Since capability is a wash, I routed based on preference fit: Avocet wants this kind of task, Willet doesn't. Routing the generative work to the model that prefers it is the sensible tiebreaker.
